=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:177-312 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The ShellCheck CI step only scans scripts/*.sh, leaving the new SessionStart hook scripts outside lint coverage.
  WHY: Every reviewer identified the same glob gap; some call it low-risk hardening, while others note future shell regressions could ship uncaught.
- .claude/hooks/session-start.sh:36-54 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: extract_repo_slug accepts non-GitHub remotes and can derive a plausible owner/repo from them.
  WHY: Reviewers note this can send gh run list -R to the wrong place and revive the misleading actions:read probe failure.
- .claude/hooks/session-start.sh:44-95 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: When slug extraction returns empty, verify_token logs a NOTE and skips the actions:read probe.
  WHY: Deepseek treats the fallback as safe, while minimax and qwen call out the silent loss of the probe.
- .claude/commands/analyze-log.md:51,53,61 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The in-repo analyze-log command still hardcodes Repo scope to `shubhodeep1/coding-workflows`.
  WHY: Minimax reports this can steer gh commands toward the wrong repo scope despite the added -R guidance.
- .claude/commands/investigate-issue.md:50,52,60 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The in-repo investigate-issue command still hardcodes Repo scope to `shubhodeep1/coding-workflows`.
  WHY: Same issue as analyze-log; minimax says models may use the hardcoded scope instead of the session-derived repo.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/analyze-log.md | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The template analyze-log command omits the new "Always emit the full Output Format" rule.
  WHY: Moonshot and z-ai report the rule is absent from the synced template, and deepseek calls the omission technically true but not practically harmful.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/investigate-issue.md | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The template investigate-issue command omits the new "Always emit the full Output Format" rule.
  WHY: Same omission as analyze-log; reviewers disagree only on whether it is a practical defect.
- workflow-templates/.claude/settings.json:8 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The SessionStart command string embeds `"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"` in JSON in a way that will not expand as intended.
  WHY: Moonshot says the literal quoted variable would make the hook command resolve to an invalid path and fail in consumer repos.
- .claude/commands/analyze-log.md:~61 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The in-repo analyze-log Rules section buries the `-R` guidance inside a longer bullet instead of making it a standalone rule.
  WHY: Qwen says models can miss the requirement and emit bare gh commands.
- .claude/commands/investigate-issue.md:~60 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The in-repo investigate-issue Rules section buries the `-R` guidance inside a longer bullet instead of making it a standalone rule.
  WHY: Qwen says models can miss the requirement and emit bare gh commands.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/analyze-log.md:121-145 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The template analyze-log Rules section still lacks a standalone `-R` mandate and leaves the guidance buried in prose.
  WHY: X-ai and z-ai both report that the guidance is easier for models to miss when it is not promoted to a separate rule.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/investigate-issue.md:121-145 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The template investigate-issue Rules section still lacks a standalone `-R` mandate and leaves the guidance buried in prose.
  WHY: Same issue as analyze-log; the `-R` requirement is present but not elevated to a distinct rule.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/analyze-log.md | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The template analyze-log command still hardcodes `shubhodeep1/coding-workflows` as the repo scope / upstream default.
  WHY: Reviewers say consumer-synced prompts inherit the upstream slug and can send gh calls to the wrong repository.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/investigate-issue.md | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The template investigate-issue command still hardcodes `shubhodeep1/coding-workflows` as the repo scope / upstream default.
  WHY: Same consumer-synced upstream default problem as analyze-log.
- .claude/hooks/session-start.sh:~50 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The awk-based field split is fragile around remotes that include a port number.
  WHY: Qwen flags this as a potential edge case, though they also note it is probably not an actual bug and existing tests cover the intended proxy URL shape.
- tests/test_session_start_extract_repo_slug.py | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The new test file only exercises extract_repo_slug in isolation and does not cover verify_token end-to-end.
  WHY: Qwen says the integration flow that actually drives gh run list -R remains untested.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:307-312 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The ShellCheck step only iterates over scripts/*.sh, so the new hook scripts are outside CI lint coverage.
  WHY: The hook files are small and contract-tested, but this still leaves shell regressions uncaught.
- .claude/hooks/session-start.sh:44-49 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: extract_repo_slug accepts non-GitHub remotes and can return a plausible slug from them.
  WHY: Deepseek says this is a low-practical-impact design limitation, but the resulting gh probe can still be misleading.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/analyze-log.md and workflow-templates/.claude/commands/investigate-issue.md | severity=low | confidence=1
  PROBLEM: The template command files do not have the "Always emit the full Output Format" rule that was added to the in-repo versions.
  WHY: Deepseek calls this technically true but not a practical defect for the read-only template commands.
- .claude/hooks/session-start.sh:47-49 | severity=low | confidence=1
  PROBLEM: If no origin remote is present, the hook can’t derive `<owner>/<repo>` and skips the actions:read probe.
  WHY: Deepseek treats the empty-remote path as a safe fallback with a NOTE and no runtime failure path.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:307-312 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The CI ShellCheck step only scans scripts/*.sh, leaving .claude/hooks/session-start.sh and workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/session-start.sh unlinted.
  WHY: A future shell bug in session-start.sh would not be caught before shipping.
- .claude/hooks/session-start.sh:44-49 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: extract_repo_slug accepts remotes like GitLab/Bitbucket URLs and can still return a plausible-looking owner/repo slug.
  WHY: That can cause gh run list -R to probe the wrong repository and look like an actions:read problem.
- .claude/commands/analyze-log.md:51,53,61 and .claude/commands/investigate-issue.md:50,52,60 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Both in-repo commands still hardcode `shubhodeep1/coding-workflows` as the repo scope/default.
  WHY: Minimax says models can follow the hardcoded repo scope instead of the session-derived repo context.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/analyze-log.md and workflow-templates/.claude/commands/investigate-issue.md | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The template command files still hardcode `shubhodeep1/coding-workflows` as the upstream repo reference.
  WHY: Minimax says consumer-synced templates carry the upstream slug into consumer repos and point gh at the wrong repository.
- .claude/hooks/session-start.sh:44-49 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The slug extraction helper returns empty output for malformed remotes without warning.
  WHY: Minimax says malformed remotes silently skip the actions:read probe, so the session continues without the intended auth check.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

  PROBLEM: The template command files are missing the "Always emit the full Output Format" rule that exists in the in-repo versions.
  WHY: Moonshot says consumer repos synced from the templates can lose the full-report requirement and produce bare responses.

- .claude/hooks/session-start.sh:44-52 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: extract_repo_slug accepts non-GitHub URLs and can produce a plausible slug from them.
  WHY: Moonshot says the subsequent gh run list -R probe would then fail confusingly and undermine the clarity of the new auth check.
